judge.reasoning:
This is a genuinely presentation-ready report that closely tracks the business brief for a bilingual preschool.

SECTION RELEVANCE (9): Every section maps directly to a stated need. Section 1 frames the county opportunity via Hispanic share, limited-English rate, labor force participation (a smart driver of childcare demand for "working parents"), and age. Section 2 isolates heritage-language corridors, Section 3 the affluent English-speaking "bilingual advantage" segment — precisely the two customer halves in the brief. Section 4 triangulates under-10 density, 30s cohort, and married-household stability. Section 5 synthesizes into a ranked shortlist. Nothing is filler; the only minor gap is no explicit treatment of lease/commercial-cost feasibility despite a stated $6k–9k lease budget, which is arguably outside available demographic data.

NARRATIVE QUALITY (9): Specific, data-anchored, and actionable. It resists generic language: it distinguishes heritage-market vs. enrichment-market positioning, recommends Spanish-first collateral in 77036/77074, flags that top-income inner-loop ZIPs (77005, 77006, 77002) lack children and are dominated by never-married singles, and gives a concrete two-format footprint recommendation (flagship in 77089/77095, satellite in 77081/77060/77036). Narrative numbers match the chart data.

DATA PLAUSIBILITY (9): Values are realistic for Houston. 77012 (East End) ~91% Hispanic, 77005 (West U) ~63% at $150k+, 77036 (Sharpstown) high limited-English, 77002 dominated by young singles — all ring true. County median income ~$72k, median age ~34.6, and 42.8% Hispanic are all accurate for Harris County. Under-10 shares (2.7–18.4%) are sensible. Home_ownership_rate is null, a minor data gap.

VISUALIZATION APPROPRIATENESS (9): Bubble charts correctly used for 3–4 dimensional trade-offs (Hispanic share × limited-English × population × income/child-density); bar charts for categorical ZIP comparisons; histograms for the distribution of under-10 share across ZIPs; pie for racial composition (defensible as parts-of-whole). Good matches throughout.

TOOL SELECTION (9): Metrics chosen are well-targeted: Hispanic %, limited-English %, income distribution ($150k+/$100k+), under-10 age share, 30s cohort, married-household share, labor force participation. This is the right battery for a working-parent bilingual preschool. Slight ding: the addressable population is ages 1-6 but only under-10 is available as proxy (acknowledged), and no explicit fertility/household-with-children metric.

OVERALL (9): Coherent, insightful, and directly decision-useful — it hands the owner a ranked, segmented location strategy. Held back from a 10 by the null home-ownership field and the absence of any lease-cost/commercial-feasibility layer given the explicit budget.
